chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a man who becomes junub and does not find water, he said: "He performs tayammum with earth; then when he finds water, let him perform ghusl, and he does not repeat the salat (prayer)."

And about a man who passes by a well while he does not have a bucket with him, he said: "It is not upon him to enter the well, because the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth; so let him perform tayammum."

And about a man who becomes junub while he has with him only the amount of water sufficient for the wudu (ablution) of the salat (prayer): should he perform wudu with the water or perform tayammum? He said: "No; rather, he performs tayammum. Do you not see that only half of the wudu has been appointed upon him?"

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.دَلْوٌ: a bucket used to draw water
key_terms.فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ: let him perform ghusl upon finding water
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.ٱلصَّعِيدِ: earthly surface or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), here mentioned in relation to prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if water is unavailable or inaccessible for purification before salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on tayammum for a person in janabah when water is unavailable or practically inaccessible. It states that tayammum suffices for salat (prayer), that the prayer need not be repeated after later finding water, and that even limited water insufficient for ghusl is not to be used for wudu in this case.
